domain-swapped variants still explained by: amortized inference / test-time scaling / search-vs-learning evaluation
claiming a new structural boundary without resolving the recorded same-information exact reduction test
blocked_objects.strongest_reduction: amortized inference / test-time scaling / search-vs-learning evaluation
blocked_objects.exact_reduction_test: Match raw VLA and skill-harness candidate sets on diversity, mean success, and verifier availability; if raw-VLA selection/voting no longer underperforms direct execution or skill-harness selection no longer outperforms after this matching, the layer-boundary claim is falsified.
evidence_claims: Full SHAPER reaches 49.8% micro and 42.9% macro accuracy versus 32.5%/31.2% for the Seed Agent and 41.1%/38.6% for Skill Evolution.
VLA-level MG-Select and VOTE reach 21.38% and 22.00%, below direct VLA execution, while their seed-agent counterparts reach 24.38% and 23.50%, below the unscaled Seed Agent.
blocked_objects.problem_text: A tied-budget inversion: test-time selection helps skill-harness execution but harms direct VLA execution A layer-dependent method-boundary phenomenon for frozen-model embodied agents: under a tied candidate budget, selection and voting over raw VLA trajectories degrade success relative to direct execution, whereas selection/evolution over externalized skill-harness units improves success; the boundary is determined by whether candidates are composable, verifiable, contract-bearing units rather than raw motor trajectories. For a frozen VLM/VLA model and fixed embodied benchmark, if k candidates are sampled under the same compute budget, majority vote or verifier-free selection over raw VLA action trajectories will underperform direct execution, while the same selection/voting budget over skill-harness-mediated candidates will outperform direct/seed execution; the sign will remain after matching candidate diversity and mean single-candidate success, and will disappear if skill-harness candidates are flattened into unstructured text or raw trajectories.
blocked_objects.reason: The source grounding and lane contract are fully satisfied. However, under the Reduction Falsifiability Contract, the candidate collides with the mature theory of persistent-update-vs-test-time-compute (test-time scaling). The candidate proposes that test-time selection/voting systematically inverts its sign of improvement depending on the representation layer (raw VLA vs. skill-harness). While the candidate provides a falsifier matching candidate sets on diversity, mean success, and verifier availability, whether generic test-time scaling variables with structural constraints (like candidate quality, redundancy, and verifier availability) fail to predict this sign reversal remains unresolved. Because the exact reduction against generic test-time-scaling models is not definitively resolved as non-expressible, the review mandates a BLOCK under the NEEDS_EXACT_REDUCTION_TEST protocol.
blocked_objects.reopen_only_if: New primary evidence directly instantiates the recorded exact reduction test under matched information and leaves a residual prediction the named mature reduction cannot express; new wording, a new application domain, or an unexecuted proposed falsifier does not reopen this basin.

avoid: paraphrase-only variants of: Noncompensatory Scalar Collapse in Self-Evolving Agent Evaluation Loops
combining heterogeneous failures without one explicitly shared bounded operational condition
using a generic optimizer/model-capability story as a convergent-failure object without a common measured failure variable
blocked_objects.lane_contract_reason: The CONVERGENT_FAILURE lane contract requires two independent method families to fail quantitatively under the same bounded operational condition. The candidate provides grounded failures in two different domains (symbolic regression and customer support) but fails to establish a shared operational condition; they operate under different metrics, environments, and task structures. Therefore, the required_lane_evidence 'shared_condition' is not genuinely satisfied.
evidence_claims: Mean NMSE in symbolic regression can be dominated by a few catastrophic extrapolation failures, so the paper emphasizes Acc@0.01 and OOD Acc@0.01; Physics remains volatile due to oscillatory structure and phase-sensitive extrapolation.

Collapsing all evaluation signals into a single overall score performs worst and obscures critical failure modes; removing response groundedness causes the largest drop in alignment with human labels.
blocked_objects.problem_text: Noncompensatory Scalar Collapse in Self-Evolving Agent Evaluation Loops A loop-control scalar score S = aggregate(e_1,...,e_k) that is used to route proposals, distill memory, or update workflows, where one or more evidence dimensions e_j are noncompensatory: a catastrophic value on e_j cannot be repaired by gains on other dimensions, yet S can remain acceptable and therefore causes the self-evolving loop to select, retain, or amplify a catastrophic mode. For a self-evolving loop whose update rule depends only on scalar S, there exists a noncompensatory evidence dimension e_j and candidate family C such that: (1) S(C) is above the selection threshold despite catastrophic e_j(C); (2) C is selected or retained more often than a modular/evidence-view baseline under identical per-dimension evidence; and (3) repeated scalar-controlled updates reduce the probability that e_j-relevant evidence is routed into memory or future evaluation, producing increasing catastrophic-mode share over iterations.
blocked_objects.reason: Although source grounding is verified for both facts, the lane contract fails because the candidate does not establish a genuinely shared operational condition between symbolic regression and customer support evaluation. The failures are independently observed but do not meet the CONVERGENT_FAILURE machine contract.
blocked_objects.reopen_only_if: New primary evidence supplies the missing lane-contract elements explicitly (shared bounded condition, common failure object, and correctly typed evidence roles) and the resulting formulation still leaves a same-information residual beyond the recorded strongest reduction.

avoid: paraphrase-only variants of: Fixed-contract planner-executor granularity mismatch as a structural failure regime in hierarchical VLA manipulation
combining heterogeneous failures without one explicitly shared bounded operational condition
using a generic optimizer/model-capability story as a convergent-failure object without a common measured failure variable
blocked_objects.lane_contract_reason: The CONVERGENT_FAILURE lane contract is not met: source_a is incorrectly assigned the role EMPIRICAL_FACT while its evidence text is an operational assumption, and source_b's claim extrapolates beyond the supplied evidence. Furthermore, the irreducible object attempts to redefine the operationalization into an ungrounded 'fixed contract' rather than measuring a shared observable, failing the required_machine_contract.
evidence_claims: HiRoC reports that its planner consistently achieves near-perfect accuracy across episodes of different lengths, while RoboBrain2 fails to generate accurate plans under the same settings.

Before RL tuning, the executor cannot effectively execute planner-generated subgoals due to distribution misalignment between planner and executor, and without DM training the initial success rate is significantly lower.
blocked_objects.problem_text: Fixed-contract planner-executor granularity mismatch as a structural failure regime in hierarchical VLA manipulation A fixed-interface hierarchical VLA composition object in which planner subgoals are semantically correct but their temporal/action granularity lies outside the executor's trained action support, and the contract forbids renegotiation. The scientific target is the interface-induced executability boundary, not planner error or generic executor weakness. For a frozen semantically accurate planner and an executor RL-tuned on subgoals of granularity g0, held-out manipulation success will remain high for planner-generated subgoals whose temporal/action granularity lies within the executor's trained support and will drop sharply for semantically equivalent subgoals at granularity g1 outside that support, even when task identity, observations, and final goal are unchanged; allowing interface renegotiation or adding a granularity adapter will recover success, while additional RL only at g0 will not.
blocked_objects.reason: Source grounding fails for source_b because the claim and irreducible object depend on a fixed granularity contract that is not supported by the excerpt. Lane contract fails due to incorrect evidence roles and missing shared operationalization for the proposed failure regime.
blocked_objects.reopen_only_if: New primary evidence supplies the missing lane-contract elements explicitly (shared bounded condition, common failure object, and correctly typed evidence roles) and the resulting formulation still leaves a same-information residual beyond the recorded strongest reduction.

avoid: paraphrase-only variants of: Capability-dependent collapse of open-ended self-evolving optimizers
combining heterogeneous failures without one explicitly shared bounded operational condition
using a generic optimizer/model-capability story as a convergent-failure object without a common measured failure variable
blocked_objects.strongest_reduction: cross-model prompt transfer / instruction following / model-artifact compatibility
blocked_objects.lane_contract_reason: The CONVERGENT_FAILURE lane contract requires two grounded empirical facts to demonstrate quantitative failure under the same bounded operational condition, naming a common failure object. The candidate extracts failures from two different artifact families and optimizers: OEO failing with medium/weak optimizers on skill improvement (arXiv:2608.09629) and a Haiku 4.5 coding agent failing to converge on network verifier extension tasks (arXiv:2608.11340). These are independent domains and interfaces; they do not share a method family nor a common failure object beyond the generic observation that weaker models perform worse on complex tasks, which violates the 'same bounded operational condition' and 'names a common failure object rather than a better-method claim' requirements.
blocked_objects.exact_reduction_test: Hold target-interaction budget and evaluation fixed while varying only whether the route is prescribed or optimizer-composed. If performance is fully explained by total compute/search quality without an interface-specific discontinuity, the baseline absorbs the claim.
evidence_claims: GPT-5.5-driven Open-Ended Optimization wins most comparisons, but delegation has a capability boundary: SkillOpt outperforms OEO with a medium optimizer, and a weak optimizer cannot operate through the unchanged OEO interface.
In self-evolving network verifiers, not every coding-agent model sufficed: runs with Haiku 4.5 as the coding agent failed to converge on any of the three model-extension tasks.
blocked_objects.problem_text: Capability-dependent collapse of open-ended self-evolving optimizers An optimizer-enactability boundary for open-ended self-improvement: under fixed objective, interactions, budget, data boundary, and evaluation, the same self-evolution interface can be enacted by a sufficiently capable optimizer but collapses for weaker optimizers, with the transition observable as non-convergence or inability to compose the improvement route rather than as a downstream task-model deficit. For a fixed self-evolution interface with unchanged objective, permissions, feedback, data boundary, and budget, there exists a capability threshold below which the optimizer cannot enact open-ended route composition: weak optimizers show non-operation or non-convergence across tasks, medium optimizers improve only under a prescribed pipeline, and frontier optimizers improve through OEO. This ordering will replicate across at least two independent artifact families (skill procedures and symbolic verifier extensions).
blocked_objects.reason: The source claims are accurately grounded in the supplied primary evidence. However, the candidate fails the CONVERGENT_FAILURE lane contract because the two empirical facts do not share an explicitly bounded operational condition; they represent isolated failures of weaker LLMs on distinct agent tasks (skill optimization vs. SMT encoding extension) rather than a convergent quantitative failure under a common operational condition with a named common failure object. Furthermore, the candidate's identified irreducible object (optimizer-capability threshold for enacting self-evolution interfaces) is a SOFT_COLLISION with known patterns of model-scaffold-enactability and persistent-update-vs-test-time-compute, as weaker models failing to operate interfaces is highly reducible to standard instruction-following and test-time compute limitations. Because the lane contract fails, the verdict is BLOCK.
blocked_objects.reopen_only_if: New primary evidence supplies the missing lane-contract elements explicitly (shared bounded condition, common failure object, and correctly typed evidence roles) and the resulting formulation still leaves a same-information residual beyond the recorded strongest reduction.

rows.original_problem: Model-trigger-skill-context acceptance object with a compositional-risk veto for evolved skill deployment.
rows.collision_reason: The original novelty bundle is occupied in pieces that together reproduce the claimed paper object: lifecycle governance already maps verification to graduated deployment permissions; dependency/context-aware skill-chain risk is explicit; conditional dormant attacks and model-dependent skill behavior are already empirical first-class objects. A new install/update/block/escalate acceptance object therefore reduces to a contextual security/utility policy unless it proves a stronger impossibility or decision-theoretic phenomenon.
rows.surviving_risk_axis: Context-dependent admissibility of the same evolved skill across target model × trigger × installed-skill/workflow context remains a useful evaluation axis, but not a standalone paper thesis under the current formulation.
strongest_same_information_baselines: Skill Trust and Lifecycle Governance gates/tiers with context-aware verification features
ChainGuard-style candidate+installed-skill context analysis followed by graduated permission assignment
generic contextual constrained decision/risk-sensitive policy using identical model/trigger/workflow/security/utility features
MASA-style model-conditioned skill adaptation plus a security gate
revival_requirements: State an ex-ante prediction that cannot be expressed by a contextual constrained policy using exactly the same model/trigger/workflow/utility/security evidence.
Show that the same skill's admissibility has a structural non-separability/impossibility property, not merely model dependence or composition dependence.
Beat lifecycle-governance and ChainGuard-derived decision rules under the same information and false-positive/utility budget.
Do not use a new scalar score, trust tier, permission tier, scanner, or hard veto as the novelty claim.
rows.cheapest_problem_falsifier: Construct the candidate's intended install/update/block/escalate labels on a small matched table, then fit or hand-compile a generic contextual constrained policy with the identical target-model, trigger, installed-skill/workflow, utility, and security observations. If it reproduces the decisions, the revised object has no irreducible paper novelty.
rows.next_action: Stop standalone SP-09. Preserve context-dependent admissibility as a risk/baseline axis for future skill-evolution papers; reopen only with a non-separability/impossibility result beyond contextual governance.

rows.original_problem: The explicit-procedure boundary of query-only skill retrieval.
rows.collision_reason: Implicit query difficulty, reasoning-enhanced query-only retrieval, task decomposition, structured multi-skill routing, query-conditional skill-set compatibility, same-capability ambiguity, and typed structural retrieval are already occupied. The original explicit-versus-implicit procedural boundary is therefore not sufficient novelty.
rows.revised_problem: Given an observable user query q and a fixed skill library L under query-only inference, is the minimally sufficient capability/skill set point-identifiable from q at all? If multiple task semantics that are observationally compatible with the same q require incompatible sufficient skill sets, retrieval is structurally non-identifiable and a system must abstain or acquire additional information rather than merely rerank more strongly.
rows.irreducible_boundary_required: The claim must be about observational non-identifiability of the sufficient skill set, not about implicit queries being harder, decomposition improving retrieval, multi-skill compatibility, same-capability representative risk, or a new clarification policy. The paper must separate 'retriever failed to infer latent steps' from 'no query-only retriever can identify one sufficient set from the available information'.
strongest_same_information_baselines: SkillWeaver / SkillReranker task decomposition and structured reranking
generic partial identification over latent task interpretations
generic clarification-need prediction / active query refinement
required_problem_revision: Define an observational equivalence relation over task semantics that produce the same available query representation and map each semantic state to a sufficient capability/skill set.
Define point-identifiable, set-identifiable, and non-identifiable retrieval cases before introducing any learned method.

Require matched examples where the observable query is held fixed or information-equivalent while compatible latent task semantics require incompatible sufficient skill sets; simple short-vs-long or explicit-vs-implicit pairs are insufficient.
Show that an oracle ranker with the same query information cannot resolve the non-identifiable cases; otherwise the issue is model quality rather than information structure.
Audit against generic selective prediction, partial identification, and clarification policies using exactly the same ambiguity set/evidence.
Do not claim task decomposition, capability reasoning, top-rank-versus-coverage metrics, or abstention itself as novelty.
rows.cheapest_problem_falsifier: Before method design, inventory existing SkillReason/SkillRet/CompSkillBench/R3-Skill/SkillResolve-style assets for query-level units where one observable or information-equivalent query admits multiple plausible task semantics with incompatible sufficient skill sets. If no such units exist, or if a generic uncertainty/clarification baseline using the same information resolves them, stop the revised problem.
rows.next_action: Run a data-only support inventory for query-level non-identifiability. Advance to method design only if nonzero matched units survive source/provenance and generic partial-identification/clarification reduction checks.

portfolio_decision: Retrospective shadow audit only: SP-09 stops standalone after direct governance/context/model-dependence collisions. SP-15 is revised from an explicit-procedure retrieval boundary to query-only sufficient-skill-set identifiability, but remains blocked from Method Design until query-level support inventory establishes nonzero observationally non-identifiable units and generic partial-identification/clarification baselines do not absorb the object. Neither shadow candidate has live Paper Design authority.
next_action: Use these outcomes only as zero-authority shadow-search feedback. Do not design a method, compile an Experiment Blueprint, mutate the canonical Problem-Gate queue, start P0, or use GPU for either candidate.
